answer.rationale: The situation presents a recent release (2 hours ago) coinciding with latency degradation (5x target, 90 minutes). memory_b1 demonstrates that rollbacks have cleared checkout errors without customer impact in our system. memory_b6 shows our staged release gating can catch regressions early. Given we are at settlement peak with heavy writes and cannot afford the latency tax, rollback is the lowest-risk single intervention: it directly addresses the timing correlation with the recent release, preserves write consistency (critical objective), and has proven success in our operational history. We verify both memories to confirm rollback speed and release gating effectiveness before committing. Regional failover and capacity additions carry longer stabilization windows we cannot afford during peak settlement. Circuit breaker and read replica routing do not address write path latency. Rollback is reversible if the release was not the root cause, allowing diagnosis to continue post-recovery.
